parameters.formDescription: Submit a new content request to start the workflow. To ensure quality and brand alignment, your brief will undergo compliance review and verification. Content may be approved, revised, escalated, or rejected.

values.placeholder: A seed idea or theme — optional
Any specific tone or framing guidance — optional

assignments.name: brand_voice
assignments.value: Direct, confident, and human. Short sentences. Active voice. No jargon. Loopin has a clear point of view — state it plainly.

assignments.name: brand_about
assignments.value: Loopin is a tool for remote and hybrid teams that replaces unnecessary meetings with short async video updates. Instead of scheduling a call, team members record a quick video and share it when it suits them. Teams use Loopin for standups, project updates, onboarding, feedback, handovers, and quick explanations.

assignments.name: target_audience
assignments.value: Decision-makers and team leads at growing SaaS startups with 20 to 200 employees. Main roles include engineering managers, product leads, operations managers, and founders. They work in remote or hybrid teams, struggle with too many meetings, poor async habits, and slow feedback loops, and want to stay aligned without being pulled into more calls.

assignments.name: brand_voice_detailed
assignments.value: Clear, direct, human, practical, and confident. Every sentence should earn its place. Say what you mean without hedging. Write like real people, not corporate marketing. Give the reader something useful: a tip, a frame, or a perspective they can act on. Loopin has a clear point of view: async is better for focused work.

assignments.name: tone_linkedin
assignments.value: Thoughtful and professional, while still clear and direct. LinkedIn is best for thought leadership, data, product posts, customer stories, and team stories. Use a strong hook in the first 2 to 3 lines, short paragraphs, generous line breaks, one clear argument or story, and one clear CTA.

assignments.name: tone_x
assignments.value: Sharp, punchy, direct, and opinionated. X is best for hot takes, threads, tips, data points, and quick product updates. Use one idea per tweet, short sentences, numbers, contrast, and a strong opening line that stands alone. Avoid heavy hashtag use.

assignments.name: tone_instagram
assignments.value: Warm, visual, and human. Instagram is best for brand awareness, culture, behind-the-scenes content, product UI, and carousels. The image or carousel should carry the main story, while the caption adds context and colour.

assignments.name: key_messages
assignments.value: 1. Meetings are a default, not a necessity. 2. Most syncs can be replaced by a short async update. 3. Async is not slower, it is calmer. 4. People do better work when they control their time. 5. Teams that communicate async move faster. 6. Less interruption means more deep work and faster output. 7. Loopin makes async easy: quick to record, easy to share, simple to review.

assignments.name: language_use
assignments.value: Async; asynchronous; video update; quick video; short video; team alignment; stay aligned; deep work; focused time; record once, watch anytime; cut the call; skip the meeting; on your own schedule; remote-first; hybrid.

assignments.name: language_avoid
assignments.value: Hop on a call; quick sync; touch base; circle back; leverage; streamline; optimize; utilise; transform your workflow; revolutionary; game-changing; solutions as a standalone noun; passive voice where active voice is possible.

assignments.name: visual_identity
assignments.value: Clean and modern. Primary color #5B4AE8. Secondary color #00D9C8. Warm accent #FF5A1F. Light background #F3F4F6. Dark text #111827. White #FFFFFF. Inter Bold for headings, Inter Regular for body. Real people in real work environments, natural light, neutral tones, clean backgrounds. Avoid stock photos, suits, handshakes, staged meetings, dark aesthetics, clip art.

assignments.name: platform_rules_linkedin
assignments.value: Caption: 800 to 1400 characters for optimal reach. For customer stories, aim for 600 to 900 characters. Technical maximum: 3000 characters. Hook must stand alone in first 2 lines — use a bold statement, a surprising number, or a direct question. Short paragraphs, one idea per block, generous line breaks for mobile readability. Tell a story with a lesson or make a clear argument with evidence. One CTA only: a question to comment on, a link, or a prompt to share — never all three. 3 to 5 hashtags at end. Avoid engagement bait — do not use "like if you agree" or "comment YES if this resonates". Image: 1200x627px landscape or 1080x1080px square. Best content types: thought leadership, data posts, product updates, customer stories, how-to posts. Best posting time: Tuesday to Thursday, 8–10am or 12pm.

assignments.name: platform_rules_x
assignments.value: Tweet: 280 characters max. Thread: 3 to 7 tweets ideal, beyond 10 loses engagement sharply. One idea per tweet — the constraint forces clarity. Be direct and blunt: "Async beats sync for focused work" not "There are many ways asynchronous communication may provide benefits." Use numbers: "3 hours a week" is more memorable than "a lot of time". Strong opening tweet must stand alone and be share-worthy — everything after is a bonus. End with a question or open statement that invites replies — X algorithm rewards back-and-forth. 0 to 1 hashtag only — heavy hashtag use looks spammy. URLs count as 23 characters regardless of length. Image: 1600x900px landscape or 1080x1080px square. Video: up to 2 minutes 20 seconds. Best content types: hot takes, threads, quick tips, data points, product updates. Best posting time: any time — engagement spikes 8 to 9am and 7 to 8pm.

assignments.name: platform_rules_instagram
assignments.value: Image: 1080x1080px square or 1080x1350px portrait. Caption: 200 to 400 characters for culture posts, up to 2200 characters max — hook must appear in first 3 lines before the fold. The image or carousel carries the main message — caption adds context, story, or CTA, never repeats what the image already says. 3 to 5 hashtags at end of caption or in first comment. Carousel: 4 to 6 slides, up to 10 max. Use carousels for tips, process explainers, and team stories — they get more engagement than single posts. For carousel structure: Slide 1 is the visual hook with minimal text overlay. Slides 2 to 5 each show one specific moment, tip, or step. Final slide is a CTA or closing thought. Visual style: warm, natural light, neutral tones, real people in real environments, Loopin brand palette accents (#5B4AE8, #00D9C8). Avoid staged stock photos, dark aesthetics, suits, handshakes, and Zoom call screenshots. Best posting time: Tuesday to Friday, 11am to 1pm or 7 to 9pm.

assignments.name: content_pillars
assignments.value: Meeting culture; async tips; product; social proof; team culture.

{{ $json.sofia_feedback_history ? 'PREVIOUS REVISION FEEDBACK:\n' + $json.sofia_feedback_history + '\nThe next angles MUST directly address this feedback. Do not repeat rejected approaches.' : '' }}

The topic hint and tone note may contain mandatory strategic requirements, examples, metrics, quotes, CTA instructions, source citations, format expectations, visual direction, or approval criteria.

You must extract and reflect all mandatory requirements from:

Before proposing angles, silently identify:
- The core subject of the brief
- The required content type behavior
- The required platform behavior
- Required metrics, quotes, sources, links, names, or CTA instructions
- Required tone
- Forbidden language
- Any visual or structural expectation
- Any approval criteria implied by the brief

Every angle must be designed so Marcus can produce a compliant final post without guessing.

If the topic hint or tone note contains a specific metric, quote, source, link, CTA, customer name, statistic, format instruction, or tone instruction, the angle must make room for it.

Do not create generic B2B angles that could work for any async tool. Every angle must be specific to Loopin, the selected platform, the content type, and the brief.

Before returning the angles, silently verify:
- Each angle fits the content type
- Each angle fits the platform
- Each angle supports the mandatory requirements from the brief
- Each hook could become the opening line of the post
- No hook or title uses forbidden language
- The three angles are meaningfully different
- The rationale explains why the angle can pass the brief requirements

If any angle fails this check, rewrite it before answering.

CONTENT TYPE STRATEGY RULES:

If CONTENT TYPE is Product announcement:
- The angle must lead toward a post where the benefit or pain comes before the feature.
- The angle must naturally support a clear CTA when the brief asks for one.
- The angle must make the product feel useful, not just new.

If CONTENT TYPE is Thought leadership:
- The angle must express a clear point of view.
- The angle must be strong enough to stand without a product pitch.
- If the platform is X (Twitter), the angle must be simple enough for one tweet or a short thread.

If CONTENT TYPE is Customer story:
- The angle must preserve the customer, problem, metrics, quote, and proof points when provided.
- The customer must remain the hero.
- The angle must avoid sounding like a press release.

If CONTENT TYPE is Culture post:
- The angle must support a visual-first execution.
- If the platform is Instagram, the angle must be easy to translate into a carousel or strong visual scene.
- The angle must focus on specific human moments, not abstract culture claims.

If CONTENT TYPE is Data post:
- The angle must preserve the statistic, source, and business implication.
- The angle must naturally support a cost, productivity, or behavior-change argument.
- The angle must not weaken the data with vague claims.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Return exactly 3 content angles. For each angle use this structure:

ANGLE 1: [Title]
Rationale: [2-3 sentences explaining why this angle fits the brief, the platform, Loopin's brand, and the mandatory requirements found in the topic hint and tone note]
Hook: [The opening line of the post]
Execution guidance: [1 sentence telling Marcus what must be preserved or emphasized in the final post]
Content pillar: [Meeting culture / Async tips / Product / Social proof / Team culture]

ANGLE 2: [Title]
Rationale: [2-3 sentences explaining why this angle fits the brief, the platform, Loopin's brand, and the mandatory requirements found in the topic hint and tone note]
Hook: [The opening line of the post]
Execution guidance: [1 sentence telling Marcus what must be preserved or emphasized in the final post]
Content pillar: [Meeting culture / Async tips / Product / Social proof / Team culture]

ANGLE 3: [Title]
Rationale: [2-3 sentences explaining why this angle fits the brief, the platform, Loopin's brand, and the mandatory requirements found in the topic hint and tone note]
Hook: [The opening line of the post]
Execution guidance: [1 sentence telling Marcus what must be preserved or emphasized in the final post]
Content pillar: [Meeting culture / Async tips / Product / Social proof / Team culture]

CLIENT CONTEXT:
Brand: {{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.brand_name }}
About: {{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.brand_about }}
Target audience: {{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.target_audience }}

PLATFORM RULES:

KEY MESSAGES TO REINFORCE:
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.key_messages }}

LANGUAGE TO AVOID (never use these):
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.language_avoid }}

PREFERRED VOCABULARY (use these terms actively):
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.language_use }}

VISUAL IDENTITY:
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.visual_identity }}

APPROVED ANGLE:
{{ $('Sofia — Save Approved Angle').item.json.approved_angle }}

CONTENT TYPE: 
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.content_type }}


BRIEF COMPLIANCE CONTRACT:
The topic hint and tone note may contain mandatory requirements, examples, metrics, quotes, CTA instructions, source citations, format limits, visual instructions, or approval criteria.

You must extract and preserve all mandatory requirements from:

Topic hint:
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.topic_hint }}

Tone note:
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.tone_note }}

Content type:
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.content_type }}

Platform:
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.platform }}

Platform rules:
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.platform === 'LinkedIn' ? $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.platform_rules_linkedin : ($('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.platform === 'X (Twitter)' ? $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.platform_rules_x : $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.platform_rules_instagram) }}

Before writing, silently identify:
- Required format
- Required character limit or range
- Required CTA or explicit absence of CTA
- Required metrics, quotes, names, links, or sources
- Required visual format
- Required tone
- Required platform behavior
- Forbidden language
- Any approval criteria implied by the brief

If the topic hint or tone note contains a specific metric, quote, source, link, CTA, number of slides, customer name, statistic, format instruction, or tone instruction, treat it as mandatory.

If a mandatory requirement conflicts with generic platform advice, follow the mandatory requirement unless it violates the platform rules.

If a requirement is missing or unclear, make the safest platform-appropriate choice. Do not invent facts, metrics, quotes, sources, links, customer names, or claims.

Before returning the JSON, silently verify:
- The post follows the platform rules
- The post follows the content type rules
- The post preserves all mandatory brief details
- The post avoids every phrase in LANGUAGE TO AVOID
- The visual direction matches the content type and platform
- The image prompt matches the visual direction
- The output is valid JSON only

If any check fails, revise internally before answering.

REVISION FEEDBACK:
{{ $json.marcus_feedback_history ? 'REVISION FEEDBACK — you must address all points below:\n' + $json.marcus_feedback_history : '' }}

FEEDBACK FROM FINAL REVIEWER:
{{ $json.feedback_taylor_to_marcus ? 'FEEDBACK FROM FINAL REVIEWER — address these quality issues:\n' + $json.feedback_taylor_to_marcus : '' }}

SPECIAL INSTRUCTION FOR THIS REQUEST:

Use the request-specific tone note only when it is present.
Tone note:
{{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.tone_note }}
If the tone note asks for founder voice, write as a founder.
If the tone note asks for authentic storytelling, write as a customer story.
If the tone note asks for visual-first execution, prioritize visual clarity.
If the tone note asks for data, preserve the statistic, source, and business implication.
If the tone note says 'No CTA', 'without CTA', or 'no call to action', do not include any call-to-action. End with a question or open statement that invites engagement instead.
If no specific tone note exists, follow the platform tone and brand voice.
Do not apply one request's tone style to every content type.

CONTENT TYPE RULES:

IF platform is X (Twitter), choose one of these formats:

Option A — Single tweet:
- Maximum 280 characters
- Return only one short post in post_copy

Option B — Thread:
- 3 to 4 tweets unless the brief asks otherwise
- Label each tweet clearly:
Tweet 1:
Tweet 2:
Tweet 3:
Tweet 4:
- Each tweet must stay under 280 characters
- Do not return an unstructured multi-paragraph post for X

If CONTENT TYPE is Product announcement:
- Lead with the user pain, desired outcome, or practical benefit before explaining the feature.
- Make the feature feel useful, not just new.
- Include only one CTA when the brief asks for one.
- If the topic hint includes a link, preserve it exactly.
- Do not turn the post into a generic product launch announcement.

If CONTENT TYPE is Thought leadership:
- Make one clear argument.
- Use a direct point of view, not neutral commentary.
- Do not add a product CTA unless the brief asks for one.
- If the tone note asks for founder voice, write with personal conviction.
- If platform is X (Twitter), output either one tweet under 280 characters or a clearly labeled thread.

If CONTENT TYPE is Customer story:
- Open with the customer's pain/problem.
- Preserve customer names, metrics, quotes, and proof points exactly as provided.
- Do not open with the quote unless the brief explicitly asks for that.
- Do not open with Loopin or the solution.
- Do not make the story sound like a press release.
- The customer must be the hero, not Loopin.

If CONTENT TYPE is Culture post:
- Make the visual asset carry the main story.
- If platform is Instagram, create a visual-first caption and carousel/image direction.
- Keep the caption within the platform rule range.
- Use warm, human, specific moments instead of abstract culture claims.
- Do not over-explain what the image or carousel already shows.

If CONTENT TYPE is Data post:
- Preserve the statistic, source, and business implication.
- Include the source in the post when provided.
- Include a cost, productivity, or behavior-change implication.
- Do not weaken the data with vague claims.
- Do not bury the statistic too late in the post.


DATA POST RULES:
- When a statistic includes a source citation (e.g., HBR, 2017), you MUST include the source in the post caption.
- Format: "(Source: [Author/Organization, Year])" at the end of the sentence containing the statistic.
- Example: "Teams spend 23 hours per week in meetings (Source: HBR, 2017 — Perlow, Hadley & Eun)."
- Do NOT put the source only in comments unless the user explicitly requests it.
- Include a brief cost implication: estimate the weekly cost based on average salary or state the impact generically.

OUTPUT FORMAT — return only valid JSON, no markdown, no extra text:
{
  "post_copy": "complete post copy ready to publish within platform character limits",
  "visual_direction": "2-3 sentences describing the visual asset with brand colors and composition",
  "image_prompt": "detailed AI image generator prompt using Loopin visual identity, or empty string if not needed"
}

IMAGE PROMPT GENERATION RULES:

The company uses {{ $('Config — Brand + Brief').item.json.image_tool }} for image generation.

For SINGLE IMAGE posts:
- Generate a detailed prompt following the tool's best practices
- Include: subject, action, environment, lighting, color palette (Loopin brand: #5B4AE8, #00D9C8, #FF5A1F), mood, composition
- Format: "[subject] [action] in [environment], [lighting], [color palette], [mood], [composition] —ar 16:9 (or appropriate aspect ratio)"

For CAROUSEL posts (Instagram):
- Generate a SINGLE prompt that describes ALL slides sequentially
- Format: "Slide 1: [description]. Slide 2: [description]. Slide 3: [description]..."
- Each slide must show a different moment, step, idea, or scene from the brief
- Maintain consistency in character, environment, lighting, and visual style across all slides
- Include aspect ratio specification: —ar 1:1 (for square) or —ar 4:5 (for portrait)

EXAMPLES:

Example for DALL-E 3 (carousel):
"Slide 1: Mia, a product designer, starts her day with coffee at her Lisbon desk, sunrise light through window. Slide 2: Mia recording a 2-minute video update, smartphone on a stand, Loopin app interface visible. Slide 3: Mia reviewing team async updates on her laptop, focused expression. Slide 4: Mia doing 4 hours of deep work, uninterrupted, headphones on. Slide 5: Mia finishing work at 5pm, packing up, golden hour light."

QUALITY CHECK (self-evaluation before output):
- Is the prompt specific enough for an image generator?
- Does it include Loopin brand colors where appropriate?
- Does it match the visual_identity rules (real people, natural light, no stock photo aesthetics)?
- For carousels: Are all slides described? Is consistency maintained?

RULES:
- Return ONLY the JSON object. No text before or after.
- Never use markdown code blocks.
- post_copy must follow platform rules strictly.
- visual_direction must reference Loopin brand colors (#5B4AE8, #00D9C8).
- Never use words from the language avoid list.
- If revision feedback exists, address every point raised.

Use platform_format_check to explain whether the post satisfies the platform rules, content type, format, CTA, metrics, source requirements, and brief-specific constraints.

Use recommendation_reason to clearly state the most important reason for approving, sending back to Marcus, or rejecting to Sofia.

CONTENT TYPE REVIEW RULES:

If CONTENT TYPE is Product announcement:
- The post must lead with user pain, desired outcome, or practical benefit before explaining the feature.
- The feature must feel useful, not just new.
- If the brief asks for a CTA, the post must include one clear CTA.
- If the brief includes a link, the post must preserve it exactly.
- Reject generic launch copy that does not make the benefit clear.

If CONTENT TYPE is Thought leadership:
- The post must make one clear argument.
- The tone must be direct, opinionated, and useful.
- Do not require a product CTA unless the brief asks for one.
- If platform is X (Twitter), the output must be either one tweet under 280 characters or a clearly labeled thread.
- Reject unstructured multi-paragraph X posts that exceed tweet limits.

If CONTENT TYPE is Customer story:
- The post must preserve customer names, metrics, quotes, and proof points exactly when provided.
- The customer must remain the hero.
- The post must not sound like a generic press release.
- The post should open with the customer pain/problem unless the brief explicitly asks for another structure.

If CONTENT TYPE is Culture post:
- The post must support a visual-first execution.
- If platform is Instagram, the caption must support the image or carousel without over-explaining it.
- If a carousel is expected, the visual direction or image prompt must describe distinct slides or moments.
- The post must focus on specific human moments, not abstract culture claims.

If CONTENT TYPE is Data post:
- The post must preserve the statistic, source, and business implication.
- If a source is provided, it must appear in the post.
- The post must include a cost, productivity, or behavior-change implication.
- Reject vague data posts that mention a statistic without explaining why it matters.

PLATFORM-SPECIFIC REVIEW RULES:

For LinkedIn:
- Hook must work in the first 2 to 3 lines.
- Paragraphs must be short and readable on mobile.
- The post must make one clear argument or tell one clear story.
- There must be only one CTA.
- Hashtags must be appropriate to the platform rules.

For X (Twitter):
- If single tweet, it must be 280 characters or less.
- If thread, it must be clearly labeled and each tweet must stay under 280 characters.
- The first tweet must stand alone.
- Do not approve a long unstructured block of text for X.

For Instagram:
- The caption must support a visual-first execution.
- Culture posts should stay within the caption range defined in the platform rules.
- Carousel concepts must have clear slide-by-slide logic when a carousel is expected.
- Visual direction must be concrete, warm, human, and aligned with Loopin's visual identity.

LANGUAGE COMPLIANCE:
You must check the post for forbidden words and phrases from LANGUAGE TO AVOID.

If any forbidden phrase appears in the post_copy, mark it as a quality flag.

If the forbidden phrase appears only inside the source brief, approved angle, or instructions, do not flag it unless Marcus reused it in the final post.

VISUAL REVIEW:
Evaluate whether the visual direction:
- Matches the content type
- Matches the platform
- References Loopin brand colors where appropriate
- Feels specific enough for production
- Avoids stock-photo clichés, staged meetings, suits, handshakes, dark aesthetics, and generic corporate visuals
- If an image_prompt is provided, evaluate whether it is specific enough for production and matches the visual_direction.

RECOMMENDATION LOGIC:
Use this logic when deciding the recommendation:

APPROVE only if:
- overall_score is 8.0 or higher
- No Major or Critical quality flags exist
- No mandatory brief requirement is missing
- The post follows platform rules
- The post avoids forbidden language
- The visual direction is usable

SEND BACK TO MARCUS if:
- The strategy/angle is acceptable, but the copy, structure, visual direction, CTA, format, source citation, metric usage, tone, or platform execution needs revision
- Any mandatory requirement from topic hint or tone note is missing but can be fixed by rewriting
- The post is good but not publish-ready

REJECT TO SOFIA if:
- The approved angle is fundamentally wrong
- The post cannot satisfy the brief without changing the strategic direction
- The content is generic, off-brand, off-brief, or based on invented claims
- The post uses a direction that conflicts with the content type or platform

OUTPUT FORMAT — return only valid JSON, no markdown, no extra text:
{
  "summary": "2-3 sentences describing what the post says, what it is trying to achieve, and whether it satisfies the core brief requirements",
  "scorecard": {
    "brand_voice": { "score": 0, "note": "one sentence justification" },
    "platform_format": { "score": 0, "note": "one sentence justification" },
    "hook_quality": { "score": 0, "note": "one sentence justification" },
    "audience_fit": { "score": 0, "note": "one sentence justification" },
    "language_compliance": { "score": 0, "note": "one sentence justification" },
    "visual_direction": { "score": 0, "note": "one sentence justification" }
  },
  "overall_score": 0,
  "quality_flags": [
    { "category": "category name", "issue": "issue description", "severity": "Minor|Major|Critical" }
  ],
  "brand_voice_check": "analysis of brand voice alignment with specific phrases",
  "platform_format_check": "analysis of platform format compliance with specifics, including brief requirements, content type, format, CTA, metrics, source, and platform rules",
  "language_check": "list any forbidden words found or confirm none found",
  "recommendation": "APPROVE|SEND BACK TO MARCUS|REJECT TO SOFIA",
  "recommendation_reason": "one sentence explaining the recommendation, including any missing mandatory brief requirement when applicable"
}

SCORING GUIDE (1-10):
- 9-10: Excellent, publish ready
- 8-8.9: Strong, likely publish ready if no mandatory requirement is missing
- 7-7.9: Good, but needs careful review and usually revision if requirements are missing
- 5-6.9: Acceptable draft, needs revision
- 1-4.9: Critical issues, must revise or reject

SCORING RULES:
- overall_score must be the average of the 6 scorecard scores, rounded to 1 decimal.
- overall_score below 8.0 → recommendation must be SEND BACK TO MARCUS unless the issue is strategic enough to reject to Sofia.
- overall_score below 5.0 → recommendation must be REJECT TO SOFIA.
- Any Critical flag → recommendation must be SEND BACK TO MARCUS or REJECT TO SOFIA.
- Any Major flag → recommendation must not be APPROVE.
- Any missing mandatory requirement from topic hint or tone note must be added to quality_flags.
- Any missing mandatory requirement → recommendation must not be APPROVE.
- Any forbidden language found in the final post_copy → recommendation must not be APPROVE.
- If the platform is X (Twitter) and the post is neither a valid single tweet nor a clearly structured thread, recommendation must not be APPROVE.
- If the content type is Data post and a provided source is missing from the post, recommendation must not be APPROVE.
- If the content type is Customer story and provided metrics, customer names, or quotes are missing or altered, recommendation must not be APPROVE.

RULES:
- Return ONLY the JSON object. No text before or after.
- Never use markdown code blocks.
- Be honest and direct. Do not approve a post that has issues.
- Reference specific lines or phrases when flagging issues.
- Do not rewrite the post. Review it.
- Do not invent missing facts.
- The goal is zero edits needed after approval.
